chapter: Earl Hines, Chicago and later gigs
title: Hearing Lester Young at the Cotton Club in Minneapolis
summary: They urged Hines to hire a tenor player in a Minneapolis club, Lester Young in tennis shoes, but Hines chose Budd Johnson because Lester reportedly did not read.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: He was very light complexion. And he just turned blue all around there because he bled inwardly, you know. And he died right away. They said he -- it was instant death with him. And anyway, we went on to Minneapolis and we did the show. I had a broken ankle. And we didn't -- they were short a tenor player. So, in Minneapolis there was a little band playing out at the Cotton Club. And the guy said, well, there's a good tenor player out there. Why don't you try to get him.

So, we went out there and listened to the guy. Earl -- we told Earl the guy was real good. And somebody told Earl the guy didn't read real good. So, he didn't get him. Instead he got Budd -- instead Budd Johnson. But the guy was Lester Young. That was Lester Young. And the little band he was playing out there with was a guy named Pugh played the drums, and Adolphus Allbrooks was on the bass. Lester was on tenor. I forgot the trumpet player's name, but it was his band. I can't think of his name right now, but they were at the Cotton Club in Minneapolis. This was about '34. I think it was right around '34. And the guy was Lester Young.

So, we told Earl he sure can play, but somebody came and told Earl, well, he didn't read too well. But that's when he got Budd Johnson in to take Cecil's place instead of Lester Young. That was before Lester was with Basie. Lester was playing up at Minneapolis then.
Was Budd working -- where was Budd working?

Budd was in Chicago. But Budd and Lester had jammed against each other a lot around Kansas City in earlier days. You know, Budd's a little older than me. And they jammed a lot in -- around Kansas City before. But I didn't know that them. But it was Lester. And then Earl thought Lester was kind of wierd anyway because they was wearing
tuxedos and Lester had on tennis shoes with his tuxedo. So, they thought he was a little wierd but, you know, that was Lester. That was his style.
Earl's very proper. I mean at least he is now.

Well, he sure is. Lester sure was playing then, man. Oh, whew. He was really playing then. He was -- and we told him. Said man, this guy can play. Says, yeah, but they told me he can't read. I said but you didn't try him. He never did really try the guy, you know. He said, well, I know Budd can read because he can arrange. So, we didn't -- Earl -- it was Earl's band. You couldn't argue with him about it. But Lester sure was cooking out there. Yeah, that was -- I never forgot that little club. It was the Cotton Club out in Minneapolis, out on the road.
